tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the woman wish to study architecture?

options.A: She is attracted to the beauty of modern buildings.
options.B: She is preoccupied with her dream to be an architect.
options.C: She is influenced by her father who teaches architecture.
options.D: She is drawn to its integration of design and engineering.

questions.cn: 女士为什么想学建筑？

optionsCn.A: 她被现代建筑之美所吸引。
optionsCn.B: 她一心想着成为建筑师的梦想。
optionsCn.C: 她受到教建筑的父亲的影响。
optionsCn.D: 她被建筑对设计与工程的融合所吸引。

questions.stem: How does the woman say she will overcome the difficulty in learning mathematics?

options.A: Through hard work.
options.B: With the professor’s help.
options.C: By studying the subject online.
options.D: By taking prerequisite courses.

questions.cn: 女士说她要如何克服学习数学的困难？

optionsCn.A: 靠刻苦努力。
optionsCn.B: 靠教授的帮助。
optionsCn.C: 通过在网上学习这门课。
optionsCn.D: 通过修读先修课程。

questions.stem: What does the man say about architects’ contribution to a city?

options.A: It is groundbreaking.
options.B: It is long-lasting.
options.C: It is immaterial.
options.D: It is immortal.

questions.cn: 关于建筑师对城市的贡献，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是开创性的。
optionsCn.B: 它是持久的。
optionsCn.C: 它是无形的。
optionsCn.D: 它是不朽的。

questions.stem: What subject does the man suggest the woman start with?

options.A: Economics.
options.B: Philosophy.
options.C: Computer science.
options.D: Western art.

questions.cn: 男士建议女士从哪门科目开始？

optionsCn.A: 经济学。
optionsCn.B: 哲学。
optionsCn.C: 计算机科学。
optionsCn.D: 西方艺术。

lines.t: Have you decided what you wish to study?
lines.cn: 你决定想学什么了吗？

lines.t: Yes, professor.
lines.cn: 决定了，教授。

lines.t: I wish to study architecture.
lines.cn: 我想学建筑。

lines.t: Ah, that’s a wonderful profession.
lines.cn: 啊，那是个很棒的专业。

lines.t: Why did you choose it?
lines.cn: 你为什么选它？

lines.t: I gave a lot of thought to things you said during our last discussion, and I decided architecture made the most sense for me.
lines.cn: 我仔细想了你上次谈话中说的那些，最后觉得建筑对我来说最合适。

lines.t: In particular, I’m attracted to the marriage of design and engineering.
lines.cn: 尤其是，我被设计与工程的结合所吸引。

lines.t: That’s great, but I seem to remember you were preoccupied with all the lofty mathematics.
lines.cn: 很好，不过我记得你以前很担心那些高深的数学。

lines.t: You no longer think this aspect will be too hard for you?
lines.cn: 你不再觉得这方面对你来说太难了吗？

lines.t: No.
lines.cn: 不会。

lines.t: I was doing some online research and I think I should be able to manage.
lines.cn: 我在网上做了一些研究，我想我应该应付得来。

lines.t: Math might be the toughest subject I encounter in the curriculum, but I’ll simply put in the work required.
lines.cn: 数学也许是课程里我遇到的最难的一门，但我会付出所需的努力。

lines.t: I’m certain the fruits of my labor will pay off.
lines.cn: 我相信我的付出会有回报。

lines.t: I’m sure that’s true.
lines.cn: 我相信确实如此。

lines.t: Due to its material nature, architecture is one field where you will be able to clearly witness the contribution you make to a city.
lines.cn: 由于建筑具有物质性，它是一个你能清楚看到自己对一座城市所作贡献的领域。

lines.t: And the legacies you build will last much longer than any of us mortals.
lines.cn: 而你所留下的遗产，会比我们任何凡人存在得都久远。

lines.t: Yeah, I guess that’s true too.
lines.cn: 是的，我想这也是真的。

lines.t: So what subjects do you think I should start brushing up on in preparation?
lines.cn: 那你觉得我该开始补习哪些科目做准备呢？

lines.t: I have the whole summer.
lines.cn: 我有整个暑假。

lines.t: These days, architecture is a very diverse and dynamic degree.
lines.cn: 如今，建筑是一个非常多元、动态的学位。

lines.t: Most universities will encourage you to learn different things from fields as wide-ranging as philosophy and economics.
lines.cn: 大多数大学会鼓励你学习从哲学到经济学等广泛领域的不同东西。

lines.t: Nevertheless, I would suggest you start with computer science because there will be many intricate visuals you will have to produce as part of your projects.
lines.cn: 不过，我建议你从计算机科学开始，因为你必须为项目制作许多精细的视觉图。

lines.t: Any software in particular you think I should start with?
lines.cn: 有什么软件你觉得我应该先入手吗？

lines.t: Photoshop is a good place.
lines.cn: 从 Photoshop 开始不错。

lines.t: If you aren’t yet, try to become as proficient as you can with it.
lines.cn: 如果你还不熟练，尽量把它练到尽可能精通。

lines.t: And another thing that I would recommend you learn as much as you can is fine arts, in particular, the history of Western art.
lines.cn: 我还建议你尽量多学一点美术，尤其是西方艺术史。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about Mr. Sanchez?

options.A: He has occasionally been harassed by his fans.
options.B: He has been guarded by a discreet assistant.
options.C: He is well known to the public.
options.D: He is a famous football coach.

questions.cn: 从对话中关于桑切斯先生我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他偶尔被球迷围堵。
optionsCn.B: 他由一名低调的助理保护。
optionsCn.C: 他为公众所熟知。
optionsCn.D: 他是一位著名的足球教练。

questions.stem: What will the man do if he gets the job?

options.A: Serve as a personal assistant.
options.B: Play a key role in Real Madrid.
options.C: Run common daily chores for the woman.
options.D: Help promote Mr. Sanchez’s public profile.

questions.cn: 如果得到这份工作，男士会做什么？

optionsCn.A: 担任私人助理。
optionsCn.B: 在皇家马德里发挥关键作用。
optionsCn.C: 替女士跑日常琐事。
optionsCn.D: 帮助提升桑切斯先生的公众形象。

questions.stem: What does the man say about himself?

options.A: He is honest and always tells the truth.
options.B: He once worked part-time in university.
options.C: He cares little about his working hours.
options.D: He has little previous work experience.

questions.cn: 关于他自己，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他诚实，总是说真话。
optionsCn.B: 他大学时做过兼职。
optionsCn.C: 他不太在乎工作时间。
optionsCn.D: 他几乎没有以往的工作经验。

questions.stem: Why does the man think he is a very competitive candidate?

options.A: He has a strong ability to connect with people.
options.B: He has a high proficiency in several languages.
options.C: He has a sound knowledge of sports consultancy.
options.D: He has a natural capacity to cooperate with others.

questions.cn: 男士为什么认为自己是非常有竞争力的候选人？

optionsCn.A: 他很善于与人建立联系。
optionsCn.B: 他精通好几门语言。
optionsCn.C: 他对体育咨询有扎实的了解。
optionsCn.D: 他有与人合作的天然能力。

lines.t: So as I mentioned over the phone, we are looking for someone who is very discreet.
lines.cn: 正如我在电话里提到的，我们在找一个非常谨慎、不张扬的人。

lines.t: I can’t stress this enough.
lines.cn: 这一点怎么强调都不过分。

lines.t: I fully understand.
lines.cn: 我完全明白。

lines.t: As we all know, being such a famous football player at Real Madrid, Mr. Sanchez has a very high public profile.
lines.cn: 众所周知，作为皇家马德里如此著名的足球运动员，桑切斯先生极为高调。

lines.t: This means he cannot leave the house without being recognized and harassed.
lines.cn: 这意味着他一出门就会被认出、被围堵。

lines.t: Yes, I completely understand how imperative it would be to respect Mr. Sanchez’s private life.
lines.cn: 是的，我完全理解尊重桑切斯先生私生活有多么必要。

lines.t: Good.
lines.cn: 很好。

lines.t: As his personal assistant, you would be required to run common everyday chores for Mr. Sanchez, things he cannot do himself due to his fame, like going to the supermarket or post office.
lines.cn: 作为他的私人助理，你需要替桑切斯先生跑一些日常琐事——那些因名气而他自己做不了的事，比如去超市或邮局。

lines.t: So, well, at first sight it may appear that working for a celebrity is very glamorous.
lines.cn: 所以，乍一看，为名人工作似乎非常光鲜。

lines.t: Nothing could be further from the truth.
lines.cn: 事实恰恰相反。

lines.t: I’m telling you this so that you don’t get any false expectations of what the job has to offer you.
lines.cn: 我告诉你这些，是让你不要对这份工作抱有不切实际的期待。

lines.t: Thanks.
lines.cn: 谢谢。

lines.t: I understand this too.
lines.cn: 这一点我也明白。

lines.t: This is my first job after graduating from university.
lines.cn: 这是我大学毕业后第一份工作。

lines.t: So frankly, I don’t have much prior working experience.
lines.cn: 所以坦白说，我没什么事前工作经验。

lines.t: I am, however, very excited about the prospect of joining this company and very keen to start from the bottom in whatever capacity I may be of use.
lines.cn: 不过，我对能加入这家公司非常兴奋，也非常渴望从最底层做起，不管以什么身份能派上用场。

lines.t: That’s good to hear.
lines.cn: 听你这么说很好。

lines.t: You sound very energetic.
lines.cn: 你听起来很有干劲。

lines.t: Tell me why do you think you are well suited for this job?
lines.cn: 说说你为什么觉得自己很适合这份工作？

lines.t: Well, firstly, I love football.
lines.cn: 嗯，首先，我热爱足球。

lines.t: I’m a lifelong Real Madrid supporter and go to their games every weekend I can.
lines.cn: 我是皇家马德里的终身支持者，只要能去，每个周末都去看他们的比赛。

lines.t: I would simply love to have a job where I’m involved in some capacity with Real Madrid, regardless of the position and salary.
lines.cn: 只要能以某种方式与皇家马德里有关，无论什么职位、多少薪水，我都愿意。

lines.t: And secondly, I think what this company does in sports consultancy is very cool.
lines.cn: 其次，我觉得这家公司在体育咨询方面做的事非常酷。

lines.t: And I think my language skills could prove very useful down the road.
lines.cn: 而且我认为我的语言能力以后会非常有用。

lines.t: Please tell me more about your language skills.
lines.cn: 请多说说你的语言能力。

lines.t: I am fully fluent in English and Spanish and have a working proficiency in French.
lines.cn: 我能流利使用英语和西班牙语，法语达到工作水平。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why do extreme sports appeal to many kids?

options.A: They bring more benefits to young people.
options.B: They require less supervision and training.
options.C: They are more suitable to young people.
options.D: They have fewer rules and pressures.

questions.cn: 极限运动为什么吸引许多孩子？

optionsCn.A: 它们给年轻人带来更多好处。
optionsCn.B: 它们需要的监护和训练更少。
optionsCn.C: 它们更适合年轻人。
optionsCn.D: 它们的规则和压力更少。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about risk-free activities?

options.A: They prevent kids from enjoying adventure sports.
options.B: They help kids guard against any possible injuries.
options.C: They rob kids of the chance to cultivate their courage.
options.D: They deprive kids of the opportunity to develop team spirit.

questions.cn: 关于零风险的活动，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们使孩子无法享受冒险运动。
optionsCn.B: 它们帮助孩子防范可能的伤害。
optionsCn.C: 它们剥夺了孩子培养勇气的机会。
optionsCn.D: 它们剥夺了孩子培养团队精神的机会。

questions.stem: What should parents do if they decide adventure sports are a bit too much for their kids?

options.A: Help them take up these sports when they are more mature.
options.B: Let them participate in some less risky outdoor activities.
options.C: Ask them to try some forms of indoor sports.
options.D: Introduce them to these sports step by step.

questions.cn: 如果父母觉得冒险运动对孩子来说有点过头，他们应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 等他们更成熟时帮他们开始这类运动。
optionsCn.B: 让他们参加一些风险较低的户外活动。
optionsCn.C: 让他们尝试某些形式的室内运动。
optionsCn.D: 一步一步地把这些运动介绍给他们。

lines.t: Adventure sports are undeniably attractive to many energetic and thrill-seeking kids.
lines.cn: 对许多精力充沛、追求刺激的孩子来说，冒险运动无疑很有吸引力。

lines.t: Sports like rock climbing, surfing, skiing, and mountain biking, thus have lots of appeal.
lines.cn: 因此，攀岩、冲浪、滑雪、山地骑行这类运动极具吸引力。

lines.t: They don’t have many of the rules and pressures of traditional team sports, but they still have all the benefits of outdoor physical activity.
lines.cn: 它们没有传统团队运动那么多规则和压力，却仍享有户外体育活动的全部好处。

lines.t: When properly supervised, extreme sports can be a part of a healthy, balanced life.
lines.cn: 在有适当监护的情况下，极限运动可以成为健康、平衡生活的一部分。

lines.t: Some adventure sports may be associated with high risks of injury, so it’s important for kids to figure out when to take risks, and when not to.
lines.cn: 有些冒险运动可能伴随较高的受伤风险，所以对孩子来说，弄清何时该冒险、何时不该，很重要。

lines.t: Risk-free activities deprive kids of the opportunity to test themselves and overcome their fears.
lines.cn: 零风险的活动剥夺了孩子考验自己、克服恐惧的机会。

lines.t: But to some, these very risks are what makes these sports a bad choice.
lines.cn: 但对一些人来说，正是这些风险让这类运动成了糟糕的选择。

lines.t: They say that extreme sports can often lead to devastating injuries, especially as young thrill-seekers may attempt feats that are too advanced for them.
lines.cn: 他们说，极限运动常常导致毁灭性的伤害，尤其是年轻的寻求刺激者可能尝试远超自身能力的高难度动作。

lines.t: But let’s be real.
lines.cn: 但说实在的，

lines.t: Most kids do all kinds of dangerous stuff whether you want them to or not.
lines.cn: 不管你愿不愿意，大多数孩子都会做各种危险的事。

lines.t: Adventure sports have many of the same risks and dangers, but they have an additional sense of adventure, courage and autonomy that is important to foster in young children.
lines.cn: 冒险运动有许多同样的风险和危险，但它们额外带来一种冒险感、勇气和自主性，而这些对幼儿的培育很重要。

lines.t: As always, it’s up to parents to decide what’s best for their kids.
lines.cn: 一如既往，什么对孩子最好，要由父母来决定。

lines.t: But if you do decide that adventure sports are a bit too much, do try to introduce other forms of outdoor adventures into their lives.
lines.cn: 但如果你确实觉得冒险运动有点过头，那就一定要尝试把其他形式的户外冒险引入他们的生活。

lines.t: Camping under the stars, fishing, stargazing or even just playing in the woods can help a lot in building the same sense of self-confidence and risk-taking as in adventure sports.
lines.cn: 在星空下露营、钓鱼、观星，甚至只是在树林里玩耍，都能在很大程度上帮助培养与冒险运动相同的自信和敢于冒险的精神。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why do new tech products soon become waste?

options.A: Consumers often have a craving for the latest model.
options.B: Such products tend to comprise parts that are irreplaceable.
options.C: Tech firms intentionally design products to have short lifespans.
options.D: Manufacturers use effective strategies to promote fancier products.

questions.cn: 新的科技产品为什么很快变成垃圾？

optionsCn.A: 消费者往往渴望最新型号。
optionsCn.B: 这类产品往往包含无法替换的部件。
optionsCn.C: 科技公司故意把产品设计成寿命很短。
optionsCn.D: 厂商用有效的策略推销更花哨的产品。

questions.stem: What did the French government require tech companies to do to help consumers make better choices?

options.A: Indicate the competitiveness of their products.
options.B: List a repairability score of their products.
options.C: Specify the major parts of their products.
options.D: Detail the life cycle of their products.

questions.cn: 法国政府要求科技公司做什么来帮助消费者做出更好的选择？

optionsCn.A: 标明其产品的竞争力。
optionsCn.B: 列出其产品的可维修性评分。
optionsCn.C: 注明其产品的主要部件。
optionsCn.D: 详述其产品的生命周期。

questions.stem: What should tech companies do to help ensure environmental sustainability?

options.A: Take the initiative to reduce electronic waste.
options.B: Take due caution in upgrading their products.
options.C: Invest in constructing more recycling facilities.
options.D: Substitute all toxic substances with non-toxic ones.

questions.cn: 科技公司应该做什么来帮助确保环境可持续？

optionsCn.A: 主动减少电子垃圾。
optionsCn.B: 升级产品时给予应有的谨慎。
optionsCn.C: 投资建设更多回收设施。
optionsCn.D: 用无毒物质替代所有有毒物质。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of the problem of waste?

options.A: It can be solved.
options.B: It is certain to worsen.
options.C: It will be fixed by tech companies.
options.D: It is unavoidable in the long run.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何看待垃圾问题？

optionsCn.A: 它可以被解决。
optionsCn.B: 它必然恶化。
optionsCn.C: 科技公司会解决它。
optionsCn.D: 长远看它不可避免。

lines.t: The shiny gadgets of today will be waste tomorrow.
lines.cn: 今天这些光鲜的电子设备，明天就会成为垃圾。

lines.t: Manufacturers don’t talk much about this when they announce the big new thing that will replace your mostly just as good old thing.
lines.cn: 厂商在发布将取代你那个其实同样好用的旧产品的大新品时，并不太谈这一点。

lines.t: In fact, technology firms often purposely design devices that will not last long and cannot be repaired so that consumers will have to spend their money on a new one.
lines.cn: 事实上，科技公司常常故意把设备设计得既不耐用也无法维修，好让消费者不得不花钱买新的。

lines.t: This year, the French government began requiring tech manufacturers to list a repairability score.
lines.cn: 今年，法国政府开始要求科技厂商标注可维修性评分。

lines.t: If a device can be repaired, then its life can be extended, saving consumers money and the planet the burden of so many trashed gadgets.
lines.cn: 如果一台设备可以维修，它的寿命就能延长，既为消费者省钱，也让地球少背负那么多被丢弃设备的负担。

lines.t: Equipped with this knowledge, consumers can make better choices about which products to buy.
lines.cn: 有了这些信息，消费者就能更好地选择买什么产品。

lines.t: Some 59 million tons of old TVs, computers, screens, smartphones, washers and other electronics are discarded every year.
lines.cn: 每年约有 5900 万吨旧电视、电脑、屏幕、智能手机、洗衣机和其他电子产品被丢弃。

lines.t: This waste is dangerous.
lines.cn: 这些垃圾是危险的。

lines.t: Batteries explode in recycling facilities.
lines.cn: 电池会在回收设施里爆炸。

lines.t: Toxic substances like mercury leak into soil and groundwater and disperse in the air.
lines.cn: 汞等有毒物质会渗入土壤和地下水，并散布到空气中。

lines.t: Manufacturing flat screens adds greenhouse gases to the atmosphere.
lines.cn: 制造平面屏幕会向大气排放温室气体。

lines.t: We need tech companies to take the lead to solve this problem.
lines.cn: 我们需要科技公司带头解决这个问题。

lines.t: If they won’t, governments must make them do so.
lines.cn: 如果他们不肯，政府必须强制他们去做。

lines.t: Although tech companies will often speak of environmental sustainability, many lobby against repair legislation, fearful it will eat into their profits.
lines.cn: 尽管科技公司常把环境可持续挂在嘴边，许多公司却游说反对维修立法，担心它会侵蚀利润。

lines.t: Sustainability matters, but marketable design appears to matter more to these companies.
lines.cn: 可持续固然重要，但对这些公司来说，好卖的设计似乎更重要。

lines.t: Consumers should support right-to-repair legislation.
lines.cn: 消费者应当支持“维修权”立法。

lines.t: In this world, damage is a certainty.
lines.cn: 在这个世界上，损坏是必然的。

lines.t: But we cannot leave things broken: A problem of our creation is a problem that can be fixed.
lines.cn: 但我们不能让东西一直坏着：由我们造成的问题，就是能被解决的问题。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does most cyberloafing research focus on?

options.A: How internet monitoring can be implemented.
options.B: How to encourage productive internet surfing.
options.C: How cyberloafing affects overall productivity.
options.D: How to prevent employees from cyberloafing.

questions.cn: 大多数网络摸鱼研究关注什么？

optionsCn.A: 如何实施上网监控。
optionsCn.B: 如何鼓励高产的上网行为。
optionsCn.C: 网络摸鱼如何影响整体生产力。
optionsCn.D: 如何阻止员工网络摸鱼。

questions.stem: What was the hypothesis of the speaker’s research team?

options.A: Cyberloafing is a sign of workers’ laziness.
options.B: Cyberloafing may relieve employees of stress.
options.C: Employee engagement is closely related to job satisfaction.
options.D: Overuse of social media may lead to decline in productivity.

questions.cn: 讲话者研究团队的假设是什么？

optionsCn.A: 网络摸鱼是员工懒惰的标志。
optionsCn.B: 网络摸鱼可能为员工减压。
optionsCn.C: 员工投入度与工作满意度密切相关。
optionsCn.D: 过度使用社交媒体可能导致生产力下降。

questions.stem: On what point do the results of the speaker’s study agree with other recent research?

options.A: Taking mini-breaks means better job performance.
options.B: Cyberloafing generally does more harm than good.
options.C: Worker turnover is linked to the time allowed for cyberloafing.
options.D: Employees who indulge in internet surfing are most likely to quit.

questions.cn: 在哪一点上，讲话者研究的结果与近期其他研究一致？

optionsCn.A: 短暂休息意味着更好的工作绩效。
optionsCn.B: 网络摸鱼总体弊大于利。
optionsCn.C: 员工流失与允许网络摸鱼的时间有关。
optionsCn.D: 沉迷上网的员工最可能离职。

lines.t: On average, US workers spend about 10% of their workday surfing the internet, emailing friends or shopping online.
lines.cn: 平均而言，美国员工约把工作日的 10% 时间用于上网、给朋友发邮件或网上购物。

lines.t: This behavior, called cyberloafing, is believed to cost employers up to $85 billion a year in lost productivity.
lines.cn: 这种行为被称为“网络摸鱼”，据认为每年让雇主损失高达 850 亿美元的生产力。

lines.t: The majority of cyberloafing research focuses on ways to prevent employees from engaging in this behavior through interventions such as internet monitoring and computer use policies.
lines.cn: 大多数网络摸鱼研究关注的是如何通过干预手段——如上网监控和电脑使用政策——阻止员工这么做。

lines.t: But it turns out, such behaviors may not be a sign that a worker is lazy or just wasting time.
lines.cn: 但事实证明，这类行为可能并不是员工懒惰或只是在浪费时间的标志。

lines.t: Social media use at work has been linked to higher levels of employee engagement and job satisfaction.
lines.cn: 工作中使用社交媒体已被与更高的员工投入度和工作满意度联系起来。

lines.t: New research suggests cyberloafing can help workers cope with an exceptionally stressful work environment.
lines.cn: 新研究显示，网络摸鱼能帮助员工应对压力极大的工作环境。

lines.t: But is cyberloafing actually effective at reducing employee stress levels?
lines.cn: 但网络摸鱼真的能有效降低员工的压力水平吗？

lines.t: That’s the question my research team wanted to answer in our new study.
lines.cn: 这正是我的研究团队想在新研究中回答的问题。

lines.t: Our hypothesis was that cyberloafing may serve as a mini-break, giving employees an opportunity to recover from stressful work situations.
lines.cn: 我们的假设是：网络摸鱼可能起到“小憩”的作用，给员工一个从高压工作情境中恢复的机会。

lines.t: To test this, we asked workers to complete an online survey and rank how much time they spent cyberloafing, checking non-work emails and shopping.
lines.cn: 为检验这一点，我们请员工完成一份在线问卷，评估他们花多少时间网络摸鱼、查看非工作邮件和购物。

lines.t: We also asked them to rank job satisfaction, their desire to quit, and how often they’ve experienced mistreatment at work, such as being bullied, threatened or yelled at.
lines.cn: 我们还请他们评估工作满意度、离职意愿，以及他们在工作中遭遇不当对待（如被欺凌、威胁或吼叫）的频率。

lines.t: As you might expect, we found that overall, more mistreatment at work was correlated with lower levels of job satisfaction and a greater desire to quit.
lines.cn: 如你所料，我们发现总体上工作中遭受的不当对待越多，工作满意度越低、离职意愿越强。

lines.t: More interestingly, we found that cyberloafing effectively buffered this connection.
lines.cn: 更有意思的是，我们发现网络摸鱼有效地缓冲了这种关联。

lines.t: That is, mistreated workers who spent more time surfing the web and checking emails reported higher job satisfaction and were less likely to want to quit than similar participants who didn’t cyberloaf as much.
lines.cn: 也就是说，遭受不当对待但花更多时间上网、查邮件的员工，报告的满意度更高，也更不容易想离职——相比之下，那些较少网络摸鱼的同类参与者则不然。

lines.t: This suggests that cyberloafing acts as a sort of relief valve for workers, helping them recover from stressful experiences.
lines.cn: 这表明网络摸鱼对员工起到一种减压阀的作用，帮助他们从高压经历中恢复。

lines.t: While we did not directly assess how cyberloafing affects worker performance, we believe by relieving stress it may not only reduce worker turnover, but also ultimately bolster productivity.
lines.cn: 虽然我们没有直接评估网络摸鱼如何影响员工绩效，但我们相信，通过缓解压力，它可能不仅减少员工流失，最终还能提升生产力。

lines.t: This fits with other recent research that suggests taking short breaks is associated with higher levels of daily job performance.
lines.cn: 这与近期另一项研究相吻合：短暂休息与更高的日常绩效相关联。

lines.t: That isn’t to say cyberloafing is always good.
lines.cn: 这并不是说网络摸鱼总是好事。

lines.t: Too much time spent on non-work activities likely causes performance to suffer.
lines.cn: 花太多时间在非工作活动上，很可能会让绩效受损。

lines.t: All in all, managers should be more lenient with employees.
lines.cn: 总而言之，管理者应当对员工更宽容一些。

lines.t: We believe a bit of online shopping or surfing the internet at work could make workers more productive in the long run.
lines.cn: 我们相信，工作时段稍微网购或上网，长远看可能让员工更高产。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about Nebraska City in 1854 when Julius Morton moved there?

options.A: There were no wooden buildings.
options.B: There were environmental problems.
options.C: There were no trees.
options.D: There were few settlers.

questions.cn: 关于 1854 年朱利叶斯·莫顿搬去时的内布拉斯加城，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 那里没有木制建筑。
optionsCn.B: 那里存在环境问题。
optionsCn.C: 那里没有树。
optionsCn.D: 那里定居者很少。

questions.stem: What did Julius Morton do that increased his influence in Nebraska?

options.A: He served as chairman of the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
options.B: He urged the state to start the Nebraska State Gardening Society.
options.C: He engaged himself in a large number of aesthetic projects.
options.D: He founded a newspaper and used it to promote his ideas.

questions.cn: 朱利叶斯·莫顿做了什么从而提升了他在内布拉斯加的影响力？

optionsCn.A: 他担任了内布拉斯加州农业委员会主席。
optionsCn.B: 他敦促该州成立内布拉斯加州园艺协会。
optionsCn.C: 他投身于大量审美项目。
optionsCn.D: 他创办了一份报纸并借此推广自己的理念。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say happened on April 10, 1872?

options.A: A special prize was awarded to Julius Morton.
options.B: One million trees were planted throughout Nebraska.
options.C: The state government declared it the official Arbor Day.
options.D: Nebraska earned the nickname “the Tree Planters State”.

questions.cn: 讲话者说 1872 年 4 月 10 日发生了什么？

optionsCn.A: 朱利叶斯·莫顿被授予特别奖。
optionsCn.B: 整个内布拉斯加种下了 100 万棵树。
optionsCn.C: 州政府宣布这天为官方植树节。
optionsCn.D: 内布拉斯加获得了“植树者之州”的别称。

lines.t: When Julius Morton moved to Nebraska City in 1854, he faced a problem shared by many settlers in the territory: It was a treeless plain.
lines.cn: 1854 年朱利叶斯·莫顿搬到内布拉斯加城时，面临着该领地许多定居者共同的问题：那是一片没有树的平原。

lines.t: That meant no trees for building materials, or for fuel.
lines.cn: 这意味着没有树木可作建材，也没有柴火。

lines.t: But Morton was one of the world’s first conservationists, stating, “For prosperity, we ought to plant as many forests as we have exhausted and consumed.”
lines.cn: 但莫顿是世界上最早的自然保护者之一，他说：“为了繁荣，我们种下的森林应当与我们耗尽和消耗的一样多。”

lines.t: So he started planting trees, beginning with his own land.
lines.cn: 于是他开始种树，先从自己的土地开始。

lines.t: By 1860 Morton possessed a forest of more than 300 trees.
lines.cn: 到 1860 年，莫顿拥有了一片 300 多棵树的树林。

lines.t: A few years later, he had more than 1,000.
lines.cn: 几年后，他的树超过了 1000 棵。

lines.t: As the forest grew, so did Morton’s influence in Nebraska.
lines.cn: 树林生长的同时，莫顿在内布拉斯加的影响力也在增长。

lines.t: This was largely because Morton founded the Nebraska City News, the state’s first newspaper, in which he frequently wrote editorials about the practical and aesthetic benefits of tree planting.
lines.cn: 这主要因为莫顿创办了该州第一份报纸《内布拉斯加城新闻》，他常在上面撰写社论，谈种树在实用和审美上的好处。

lines.t: He also organized the Nebraska State Gardening Society and served on the Nebraska State Board of Agriculture.
lines.cn: 他还组织了内布拉斯加州园艺协会，并在州农业委员会任职。

lines.t: While serving on the Board, Morton came up with an idea to spread his belief in tree planting statewide.
lines.cn: 在委员会任职期间，莫顿想出一个在全州推广种树理念的办法。

lines.t: On January 4, 1872, Morton drafted a resolution that April 10 be designated a day for the planting of trees in the State of Nebraska and urged people to go out and plant trees themselves.
lines.cn: 1872 年 1 月 4 日，莫顿起草了一项决议，把 4 月 10 日定为内布拉斯加州的植树日，并呼吁人们亲自出门种树。

lines.t: Morton called the special event Arbor Day as “arbor” is Latin for “tree”.
lines.cn: 莫顿把这个特别活动称为“Arbor Day”，因为“arbor”在拉丁语中意为“树”。

lines.t: The state government agreed.
lines.cn: 州政府同意了。

lines.t: And on April 10, 1872, the first unofficial Arbor Day was celebrated throughout Nebraska.
lines.cn: 于是在 1872 年 4 月 10 日，整个内布拉斯加庆祝了第一个非正式的植树节。

lines.t: Prizes were awarded to counties, cities, and individuals who planted the largest number of trees.
lines.cn: 种树最多的县、市和个人获得了奖励。

lines.t: That day, an astounding one million trees were planted in Nebraska- an average of more than six for every man, woman and child in the state.
lines.cn: 那一天，内布拉斯加种下了惊人的 100 万棵树——平均每一位男女老幼超过六棵。

lines.t: Since 1885, Nebraska has planted more than 700,000 acres of trees, earning it the nickname “the Tree Planters State.”
lines.cn: 自 1885 年以来，内布拉斯加种下了 70 多万英亩的树木，因而获得了“植树者之州”的别称。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about modern humans according to the hypothesis commonly accepted in the 1990s?

options.A: They spread across Europe and Asia in a few decades.
options.B: They lived mostly in Africa for about 200,000 years.
options.C: They preferred to live in Europe rather than in Asia.
options.D: They moved out of Africa about 60,000 years ago.

questions.cn: 根据 20 世纪 90 年代普遍接受的假说，关于现代人类我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们在几十年内扩散到欧洲和亚洲。
optionsCn.B: 他们在非洲生活了约 20 万年。
optionsCn.C: 他们更愿意住在欧洲而不是亚洲。
optionsCn.D: 他们约 6 万年前走出非洲。

questions.stem: What has called into question the “Out of Africa” model?

options.A: The discovery of two modern human teeth in China.
options.B: The traces of human migration out of Africa to Asia.
options.C: The human fossils discovered most recently in Africa.
options.D: The Luna cave in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

questions.cn: 是什么让“走出非洲”模型受到质疑？

optionsCn.A: 在中国发现的两颗现代人牙齿。
optionsCn.B: 人类从非洲迁往亚洲的痕迹。
optionsCn.C: 最近在非洲发现的人类化石。
optionsCn.D: 广西壮族自治区隆纳洞。

questions.stem: What does the speaker want to show with the example of some monkeys in Africa?

options.A: There must have been some reason for human migration.
options.B: There have been changes in animals’ living conditions.
options.C: Humans adapted themselves to the environment there.
options.D: Humans had access to abundant food sources there.

questions.cn: 讲话者想用非洲一些猴子的例子说明什么？

optionsCn.A: 人类迁徙必定有某种原因。
optionsCn.B: 动物的生存条件发生了变化。
optionsCn.C: 人类适应了那里的环境。
optionsCn.D: 人类在那里能获得充足的食物来源。

questions.stem: What question does the speaker raise close to the end of the talk?

options.A: How humans settled down on the Arabian Peninsula.
options.B: When modern humans started to disperse out of Africa.
options.C: What path modern humans took to migrate out of Africa.
options.D: Why fresh water is so important for human survival.

questions.cn: 讲话者在临近结尾时提出了什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 人类是如何在阿拉伯半岛定居下来的。
optionsCn.B: 现代人类何时开始走出非洲。
optionsCn.C: 现代人类走的是哪条路线迁出非洲。
optionsCn.D: 为什么淡水对人类生存如此重要。

lines.t: Modern humans arose in Africa about 200,000 years ago.
lines.cn: 现代人类约 20 万年前出现在非洲。

lines.t: They then spread across Europe and Asia sometime after 60,000 years ago.
lines.cn: 随后在约 6 万年之后的某个时候，他们扩散到欧洲和亚洲。

lines.t: This is the “Out of Africa” model, as it’s commonly known.
lines.cn: 这就是通常所说的“走出非洲”模型。

lines.t: In the 1990s, the hypothesis found widespread acceptance.
lines.cn: 20 世纪 90 年代，这一假说被广泛接受。

lines.t: But this popular idea is in need of revision, particularly given the number of important findings across Asia over the past few decades.
lines.cn: 但这一流行观点需要修正了，尤其是考虑到过去几十年间在亚洲取得的大量重要发现。

lines.t: For instance, many new human fossils found, particularly in China, are now dated as older than 60,000 years.
lines.cn: 例如，许多新发现的人类化石——特别是在中国——如今被测定为早于 6 万年。

lines.t: This calls into question the idea that modern humans migrated out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
lines.cn: 这让“现代人类仅在 6 万年前走出非洲”的说法受到质疑。

lines.t: Take the recent discovery of two modern human teeth found in the Luna cave in China’s Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
lines.cn: 以最近在中国广西壮族自治区隆纳洞发现的两颗现代人牙齿为例。

lines.t: When my research team and I dated these teeth, we found they were more than 70,000 years old - a situation clearly impossible if modern humans moved out of Africa only 60,000 years ago.
lines.cn: 我和我的研究团队为这些牙齿测年后，发现它们已有 7 万年以上——如果现代人类仅在 6 万年前走出非洲，这显然不可能。

lines.t: So with such findings, what happened exactly?
lines.cn: 那么有了这些发现，究竟发生了什么？

lines.t: Where does the most current data suggest we came from?
lines.cn: 最新数据表明我们来自哪里？

lines.t: The first question we should ask is why did modern humans leave Africa to begin with?
lines.cn: 我们首先要问的是：现代人类当初为什么离开非洲？

lines.t: If a population is perfectly adapted to a particular environment and has access to an abundance of resources, then there really is no reason to move or change.
lines.cn: 如果一个种群完全适应了特定环境、又能获得充足资源，那就真的没有理由迁移或改变。

lines.t: For instance, some monkeys in Africa have a set of teeth that has hardly changed over the course of millions of years, indicating that they found a place that has worked for them.
lines.cn: 例如，非洲的一些猴子拥有一套数百万年来几乎没变过的牙齿，说明它们找到了一个适合它们的地方。

lines.t: So what happened with humans?
lines.cn: 那人类又是怎么回事？

lines.t: Some researchers have suggested that population density increased to the point where smaller human groups were forced to explore new lands.
lines.cn: 一些研究者提出，人口密度增加到一定程度，迫使较小的人类群体去探索新的土地。

lines.t: Other researchers have suggested that due to major environmental events in East Africa, humans were prompted to find greener pastures.
lines.cn: 另一些研究者提出，由于东非的重大环境事件，人类被迫去寻找更肥美的草场。

lines.t: Yet another explanation could simply be that early modern human hunters were following the large animals that they relied on, and so they moved out of Africa without realizing that they were actually moving from one continent to another.
lines.cn: 还有一种解释是：早期现代人类的猎人只是在追随他们赖以为生的大型动物，于是他们走出非洲，却没有意识到自己实际上正从一个大陆走向另一个大陆。

lines.t: Humans need daily access to reliable fresh water, which appears to be absent from many coastal areas.
lines.cn: 人类需要每天获得可靠的淡水，而许多沿海地区似乎缺乏淡水。

lines.t: This brings us to another question: by which route did modern humans move out of Africa?
lines.cn: 这就引出另一个问题：现代人类是沿哪条路线走出非洲的？

lines.t: No clear route across the Mediterranean from North Africa appear to be present, so the earlier dispersals out of Africa and into Europe and Asia might have been across the Arabian Peninsula.
lines.cn: 从北非穿越地中海的清晰路线似乎并不存在，因此较早走出非洲、进入欧洲和亚洲的扩散，可能是经由阿拉伯半岛。
